issue.title: Delete all app data leaves Whitenoise singleton using a closed database pool
issue.body:
## Summary

After using Privacy & security -> Delete App Data, signing in again in the same app process can fail with:

```text
ApiError.whitenoise(message: Database error: SQLx error: attempted to acquire a connection on a closed pool)
```

This appears to happen because the Flutter app deletes all data via the existing Rust `Whitenoise` instance, but the app process keeps the same global Rust singleton alive afterward.

## Evidence

Current app flow:

- `PrivacySecurityScreen` calls `useDeleteAllData()` and passes `deleteAllData` to the destructive confirmation action.
- On success, the screen only resets Flutter auth state and routes home.
- Rust bridge `delete_all_data()` gets the existing `GLOBAL_WN` instance via `wn()?` and calls `whitenoise.delete_all_data()`.
- The app wrapper initializes `GLOBAL_WN` with `OnceCell::get_or_try_init`, so the retained instance cannot be replaced in the same process.
- Upstream `whitenoise.delete_all_data()` calls `shutdown()`, deactivates inbox/relay control, then calls `self.shared.database.close_and_delete_files().await`.
- `close_and_delete_files()` closes the SQLx pool before deleting DB files.
- Subsequent login goes through `login_start`, which uses `self.shared.database`; on the retained instance that database pool is already closed.
- Upstream already has a test comment noting: after `delete_all_data` the database pool is closed, so a fresh `Whitenoise` instance is required for subsequent logins.

## Repro

1. Run the app in the iOS simulator.
2. Sign in or create an account.
3. Go to Privacy & security.
4. Tap Delete App Data and confirm.
5. Without killing/restarting the app process, try to sign in again.

Expected: sign-in works against a freshly initialized empty local store.

Actual: sign-in can fail with `SQLx error: attempted to acquire a connection on a closed pool`.

## Likely fix direction

The app needs an explicit post-delete lifecycle step. Possible approaches:

- Reinitialize Rust after delete by replacing the app wrapper singleton with a fresh `Whitenoise` instance.
- Expose a bridge function that performs delete-all-data and reinitialization atomically from the app config.
- Force a full app-process restart or show a restart-required state after delete, if live reinitialization is not safe yet.

The important invariant is that after full data deletion, no subsequent API call should use the old `Whitenoise` instance whose SQLx pool was closed.

issue.title: Parse message link and mention tokens in chat bubbles
issue.body:
## Summary
- Add a reusable `MessageContentText` widget that renders parsed content tokens, preserves the original message text, and makes URL tokens tappable.
- Wire `ChatMessageBubble` and `WnMessageBubble` through the new text renderer so message bubbles can display tokenized links alongside existing highlight spans.
- Add widget coverage for URL rendering and tap handling, including bubble-level verification.

## Testing
- Added widget tests for tokenized text rendering and external URL launching.
- Added bubble-level tests to confirm parsed URL tokens are passed through and tappable.
- Existing validation for the affected widget paths continues to pass at the test level.

## Testing
- Added widget tests for tokenized text rendering and external URL launching.
- Added bubble-level tests to confirm parsed URL tokens are passed through and tappable.
- Existing validation for the affected widget paths continues to pass at the test level.

Release notes

Sourced from build_runner's releases.

package:build_runner v2.15.0

  • Remove --low-resources-mode as default memory usage has been improved. If you have problems with RAM usage please file an issue.
  • Remove --log-performance and --track-performance. File an issue if you have performance measurement needs not covered by the newer --dart-aot-perf.
  • Removed options can still be passed, they will be ignored with a warning.
  • Bug fix: fix crash during logging if an asset path is an invalid URI.
  • Bug fix: with --workspace the global options affecting build order were read from the wrong package. They are now read from build.yaml in the workspace root, like other global options.
  • Allow analyzer 13.0.0.

package:build_runner v2.14.1

  • Bug fix: fix crash if a package used to belong to a workspace but was removed from the workspace leaving a stale workspace.ref file.
  • Bug fix: the watch command now always does one build before exiting due to a request from another build_runner process. Fix crashes related to request before build start.

package:build_runner v2.14.0

  • Performance: further improvements to management of files for analysis for 2x faster incremental builds.
  • Performance: default to AOT compilation for commands other than run. This costs more initial startup time but gives faster builds afterwards. Fall back to JIT if the compile fails due to use of dart:mirrors. Use the --force-jit flag if you want the old default JIT builder compile. Use the --force-aot flag to turn off the fallback to JIT compile.
  • Add support for asset: scheme to the --build-filter flag. It is like package: but for the whole package, not just lib. For example, package:a/b.dart is the same as asset:a/lib/b.dart.
  • Paths specified using --build-filter when using the --workspace flag now apply to the current package, not the workspace root. Other packages must be referred to using package: or asset: schemes.
  • Add OSC 8 hyperlinks for logged input paths.
  • Better handling of deletions of files during the build: if the file is not needed ignore the deletion, if it's needed try to use the cached version, as a last resort restart the build.
  • Defer deletions of files by build_runner until the build is complete. Don't write files unless the contents changed. These reduce unnecessary work by tools that watch the filesystem.
  • --workspace flag is no longer experimental, remove the warning.
  • Add --workspace flag to clean command, use it to clear the cache used for a --workspace build.
  • Add new command stop: run dart run build_runner stop to terminate a running watch or serve command in the current package or workspace. If a build is in progress, the build will complete first.
  • Add locking: build_runner will wait for any already-running command before running. If there is an already-running watch or serve command, it will be closed after the currently-running build, as if you ran the new dart run build_runner stop.

Updates `flutter_secure_storage` from 10.0.0 to 10.1.0
Release notes

Sourced from flutter_secure_storage's releases.

v10.1.0

Android

  • Added storageNamespace option to AndroidOptions for full namespace isolation across storage instances (SharedPreferences, KeyStore aliases, config/key storage). Use this instead of sharedPreferencesName when running multiple FlutterSecureStorage instances with different cipher configurations.
  • Deprecated sharedPreferencesName in favor of storageNamespace, which provides complete isolation rather than data-only isolation.
  • Added migrateWithBackup option to AndroidOptions for crash-resistant migration. When enabled, backup copies of encrypted data are created before migration starts, allowing recovery if migration fails or the app crashes mid-migration. Works in conjunction with migrateOnAlgorithmChange.
  • Made KeyCipherAlgorithm and StorageCipherAlgorithm public enums.

Fixes:

  • Fixed crash on biometric failure (not error).
  • Fixed null safety issue in MethodRunner that could cause a crash on Android.
  • Fixed config being overwritten on initialization.
  • Fixed default Android key cipher not aligning with the Flutter default.

iOS / macOS

  • Added useSecureEnclave option to IOSOptions and MacOsOptions to store keys in the device's Secure Enclave for hardware-backed security.

Fixes:

  • Fixed kSecAttrSynchronizable being silently dropped when no access control flags are set.
  • Fixed readAll not returning Secure Enclave items correctly.

comment.body:
IMO some issues make noise in what we really want to implement soon and what we don't. I received the feedback from an external contributor that is hard to know which issues open are things we really want to have and which are not... and which ones are already fixed or which ones are not really an issue, so I'm trying to close the ones I find they are not a priority.

For me it's a bit overwhelming too to have a list of many issues open, the important ones get buried among unimportant ones. 

I feel it's easier to decide: do we want this soon (we keep it open) or not (we label it with idea and close it) than deciding "Is this p1, p2, p3 or no p at all?" And also then keeping the priorities up to date (which I'm not really sure if someone is checking and updating, I'm not)

issue.body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/c5c1a2e55045ff2c1ee8cb64efdf9cbb54632636fcb5a6926fa2848102e4f36f.png)

## What changed

This is the Flutter side of marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs#827. `rust_lib_whitenoise` now ships from whitenoise-rs as a published Flutter package on the `flutter-package` orphan branch, and this repo consumes it via a pubspec git dep. No more `flutter_rust_bridge_codegen` runs locally, no more git-rev bumps after Rust API changes.

## Removed

- `rust/`: the wrapper crate. Canonical source now in `whitenoise-rs:crates/whitenoise-frb/`.
- `rust_builder/`: cargokit and plugin shape. Bundled inside the published package.
- `flutter_rust_bridge.yaml`: codegen config. Lives in whitenoise-rs.
- `lib/src/rust/`: auto-generated dart bindings. Published in the package.
- `justfile` recipes: `generate`, `regenerate`, `deps-rust`, `test-rust`, `test-rust-quiet`, `lint-rust`, `format-rust`, `check-rust-format`, `docs-rust`, `build-rust-debug`, `clean-bridge`, `clean-rust`.

## Updated

- `pubspec.yaml`: `rust_lib_whitenoise` switches from `path: rust_builder` to a git dep on `whitenoise-rs#flutter-package`.
- All Dart imports: `package:whitenoise/src/rust/...` becomes `package:rust_lib_whitenoise/src/rust/...` (191 files mass-rewritten; `dart fix --apply` re-sorted directives across 134 files).
- `analysis_options.yaml`: dropped the `rust_builder/**` exclude and suppressed `implementation_imports` because the orphan branch deliberately exposes `src/`.
- `AGENTS.md`: setup and dev sections rewritten, rust deps/test/lint references removed, and a pointer added to whitenoise-rs as the source of truth for the Rust core.

Stats: 304 files changed, 469 insertions, 47,854 deletions (mostly the deleted wrapper and generated dart bindings).

## Verified

- `flutter pub get` resolves the new git dep cleanly (1 dep changed).
- `flutter analyze`: No issues found.
- Dart import rewrite: zero residual `package:whitenoise/src/rust` references across `lib/` and `test/`.

## Coordination with whitenoise-rs

This PR pairs with marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs#827, and order of merge matters: the whitenoise-rs PR lands (or its workflow runs via `workflow_dispatch`) so the `flutter-package` orphan branch contains the latest published package, then this PR can merge. Otherwise `flutter pub get` resolves an outdated snapshot. The wrapper sources in the orphan branch came from this branch's `rust/src/api/` (the singleton-removal refactor that is also in this branch's history).

## Why draft

The Android build script needs the follow-up above, and a manual smoke test of `flutter pub get` and `flutter analyze` from a clean clone is still pending before this is ready for review.

The colony has split the work across two burrows: one builds the bindings, the other consumes them. Less paw-ferrying for everyone.

issue.title: feat(frb): consume rust_lib_whitenoise from whitenoise-rs orphan branch
issue.body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/c5c1a2e55045ff2c1ee8cb64efdf9cbb54632636fcb5a6926fa2848102e4f36f.png)

## What changed

This is the Flutter side of marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs#827. `rust_lib_whitenoise` now ships from whitenoise-rs as a published Flutter package on the `flutter-package` orphan branch, and this repo consumes it via a pubspec git dep. No more `flutter_rust_bridge_codegen` runs locally, no more git-rev bumps after Rust API changes.

## Removed

- `rust/`: the wrapper crate. Canonical source now in `whitenoise-rs:crates/whitenoise-frb/`.
- `rust_builder/`: cargokit and plugin shape. Bundled inside the published package.
- `flutter_rust_bridge.yaml`: codegen config. Lives in whitenoise-rs.
- `lib/src/rust/`: auto-generated dart bindings. Published in the package.
- `justfile` recipes: `generate`, `regenerate`, `deps-rust`, `test-rust`, `test-rust-quiet`, `lint-rust`, `format-rust`, `check-rust-format`, `docs-rust`, `build-rust-debug`, `clean-bridge`, `clean-rust`.

## Updated

- `pubspec.yaml`: `rust_lib_whitenoise` switches from `path: rust_builder` to a git dep on `whitenoise-rs#flutter-package`.
- All Dart imports: `package:whitenoise/src/rust/...` becomes `package:rust_lib_whitenoise/src/rust/...` (191 files mass-rewritten; `dart fix --apply` re-sorted directives across 134 files).
- `analysis_options.yaml`: dropped the `rust_builder/**` exclude and suppressed `implementation_imports` because the orphan branch deliberately exposes `src/`.
- `AGENTS.md`: setup and dev sections rewritten, rust deps/test/lint references removed, and a pointer added to whitenoise-rs as the source of truth for the Rust core.

Stats: 304 files changed, 469 insertions, 47,854 deletions (mostly the deleted wrapper and generated dart bindings).

## Verified

- `flutter pub get` resolves the new git dep cleanly (1 dep changed).
- `flutter analyze`: No issues found.
- Dart import rewrite: zero residual `package:whitenoise/src/rust` references across `lib/` and `test/`.

## Coordination with whitenoise-rs

This PR pairs with marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs#827, and order of merge matters: the whitenoise-rs PR lands (or its workflow runs via `workflow_dispatch`) so the `flutter-package` orphan branch contains the latest published package, then this PR can merge. Otherwise `flutter pub get` resolves an outdated snapshot. The wrapper sources in the orphan branch came from this branch's `rust/src/api/` (the singleton-removal refactor that is also in this branch's history).

## Why draft

The Android build script needs the follow-up above, and a manual smoke test of `flutter pub get` and `flutter analyze` from a clean clone is still pending before this is ready for review.

The colony has split the work across two burrows: one builds the bindings, the other consumes them. Less paw-ferrying for everyone.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Documentation**
  * Clarified agent setup and dependency flow; added steps to refresh the Rust core consumed as a published Flutter package; updated Android/native build guidance.

* **Chores**
  * Switched native/Rust integration to a published Flutter package; simplified development and CI workflows to run Flutter-only dependency/install/test steps.

* **Refactor**
  * Updated app imports to use the new published Rust-backed Flutter package.

* **Breaking Changes**
  * Removed the autogenerated native↔Flutter bridge surface and related native build glue; upgrade/migration required.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

issue.title: feat(frb): consume rust_lib_whitenoise from whitenoise-rs orphan branch
issue.body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/c5c1a2e55045ff2c1ee8cb64efdf9cbb54632636fcb5a6926fa2848102e4f36f.png)

## What changed

This is the Flutter side of marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs#827. `rust_lib_whitenoise` now ships from whitenoise-rs as a published Flutter package on the `flutter-package` orphan branch, and this repo consumes it via a pubspec git dep. No more `flutter_rust_bridge_codegen` runs locally, no more git-rev bumps after Rust API changes.

## Removed

- `rust/`: the wrapper crate. Canonical source now in `whitenoise-rs:crates/whitenoise-frb/`.
- `rust_builder/`: cargokit and plugin shape. Bundled inside the published package.
- `flutter_rust_bridge.yaml`: codegen config. Lives in whitenoise-rs.
- `lib/src/rust/`: auto-generated dart bindings. Published in the package.
- `justfile` recipes: `generate`, `regenerate`, `deps-rust`, `test-rust`, `test-rust-quiet`, `lint-rust`, `format-rust`, `check-rust-format`, `docs-rust`, `build-rust-debug`, `clean-bridge`, `clean-rust`.

## Updated

- `pubspec.yaml`: `rust_lib_whitenoise` switches from `path: rust_builder` to a git dep on `whitenoise-rs#flutter-package`.
- All Dart imports: `package:whitenoise/src/rust/...` becomes `package:rust_lib_whitenoise/src/rust/...` (191 files mass-rewritten; `dart fix --apply` re-sorted directives across 134 files).
- `analysis_options.yaml`: dropped the `rust_builder/**` exclude and suppressed `implementation_imports` because the orphan branch deliberately exposes `src/`.
- `AGENTS.md`: setup and dev sections rewritten, rust deps/test/lint references removed, and a pointer added to whitenoise-rs as the source of truth for the Rust core.

Stats: 304 files changed, 469 insertions, 47,854 deletions (mostly the deleted wrapper and generated dart bindings).

## Verified

- `flutter pub get` resolves the new git dep cleanly (1 dep changed).
- `flutter analyze`: No issues found.
- Dart import rewrite: zero residual `package:whitenoise/src/rust` references across `lib/` and `test/`.

## Coordination with whitenoise-rs

This PR pairs with marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs#827, and order of merge matters: the whitenoise-rs PR lands (or its workflow runs via `workflow_dispatch`) so the `flutter-package` orphan branch contains the latest published package, then this PR can merge. Otherwise `flutter pub get` resolves an outdated snapshot. The wrapper sources in the orphan branch came from this branch's `rust/src/api/` (the singleton-removal refactor that is also in this branch's history).

## Why draft

The Android build script needs the follow-up above, and a manual smoke test of `flutter pub get` and `flutter analyze` from a clean clone is still pending before this is ready for review.

The colony has split the work across two burrows: one builds the bindings, the other consumes them. Less paw-ferrying for everyone.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Documentation**
  * Clarified agent setup and dependency flow; added steps to refresh the Rust core consumed as a published Flutter package; updated Android/native build guidance.

* **Chores**
  * Switched native/Rust integration to a published Flutter package; simplified development and CI workflows to run Flutter-only dependency/install/test steps.

* **Refactor**
  * Updated app imports to use the new published Rust-backed Flutter package.

* **Breaking Changes**
  * Removed the autogenerated native↔Flutter bridge surface and related native build glue; upgrade/migration required.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

issue.title: Add Chinese localizations
issue.body: ## Summary - Add Chinese fallback localization zh required by Flutter for script-specific Chinese locales - Add Simplified Chinese localization zh_Hans - Add Traditional Chinese localization zh_Hant - Regenerate Flutter localizations for the new Chinese locales ## Validation - Ran ./scripts/validate-locales-keys.sh - All locales validated successfully ## Notes - zh_Hant was translated separately for Traditional Chinese users rather than mechanically converting from Simplified Chinese. - This PR avoids unrelated generated formatting churn in existing locale files. --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added full Simplified and Traditional Chinese localizations and exposed distinct language options ("简体中文" and "繁體中文") in language settings. * **Bug Fixes** * Improved locale handling so the app treats Simplified vs. Traditional Chinese as separate, consistent choices. * **Tests** * Expanded tests to cover locale selection, display names, and notifier behavior for both Chinese variants. `Does Dart/Flutter package guidance recommend avoiding imports from another package’s `src/` directory (e.g., `package:some_pkg/src/...`), and what are the stability/semver implications?`

💡 Result:

Yes. Dart/Flutter guidance (via Dart’s pub package layout and Effective Dart) recommends that consumers should not import another package’s private implementation code from its lib/src directory (for example, importing package:some_pkg/src/...). The guidance is that those src libraries are not part of the package’s public API and may change without following semver-breaking rules. What the guidance says - Dart’s pub package layout convention states that code in lib/src is private implementation code: other packages “should never need to import src/...”, and “you should never import from another package’s lib/src directory” because those files “are not part of the package’s public API, and they might change in ways that could break your code.” [1] - Effective Dart similarly says: “DON’T import libraries that are inside the src directory of another package.” It explains that package maintainers version their package taking this convention into account, and they are “free to make sweeping changes to code under src without it being a breaking change to the package.” [2] - Dart lints/wording in the SDK ecosystem also reflect the same intent: there’s a lint rule to avoid importing outside a package’s own lib/src (i.e., don’t depend on another package’s src/private internals). [3][4] Stability / semver implications - If you import package:some_pkg/src/..., you are depending on “private implementation details,” which the guidance explicitly characterizes as not part of the package’s public API. [1] - Because it’s not treated as public API, maintainers may change src code “without it being a breaking change” (i.e., without the semver bump you’d expect if you depended only on public APIs). [2] So the practical takeaway - For semver-stable dependencies, import only the package’s public entrypoints (typically files exported from directly-under-lib “main” libraries, or other documented public libraries), not the other package’s lib/src internals. [1] - If you control the dependency package and want certain types to be used externally, export the desired files from lib (or from your public “main” library) instead of expecting consumers to import lib/src directly. issue.body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/c5c1a2e55045ff2c1ee8cb64efdf9cbb54632636fcb5a6926fa2848102e4f36f.png)

## What changed

This is the Flutter side of marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs#827. `rust_lib_whitenoise` now ships from whitenoise-rs as a published Flutter package on the `flutter-package` orphan branch, and this repo consumes it via a pubspec git dep. No more `flutter_rust_bridge_codegen` runs locally, no more git-rev bumps after Rust API changes.

## Removed

- `rust/`: the wrapper crate. Canonical source now in `whitenoise-rs:crates/whitenoise-frb/`.
- `rust_builder/`: cargokit and plugin shape. Bundled inside the published package.
- `flutter_rust_bridge.yaml`: codegen config. Lives in whitenoise-rs.
- `lib/src/rust/`: auto-generated dart bindings. Published in the package.
- `justfile` recipes: `generate`, `regenerate`, `deps-rust`, `test-rust`, `test-rust-quiet`, `lint-rust`, `format-rust`, `check-rust-format`, `docs-rust`, `build-rust-debug`, `clean-bridge`, `clean-rust`.

## Updated

- `pubspec.yaml`: `rust_lib_whitenoise` switches from `path: rust_builder` to a git dep on `whitenoise-rs#flutter-package`.
- All Dart imports: `package:whitenoise/src/rust/...` becomes `package:rust_lib_whitenoise/src/rust/...` (191 files mass-rewritten; `dart fix --apply` re-sorted directives across 134 files).
- `analysis_options.yaml`: dropped the `rust_builder/**` exclude and suppressed `implementation_imports` because the orphan branch deliberately exposes `src/`.
- `AGENTS.md`: setup and dev sections rewritten, rust deps/test/lint references removed, and a pointer added to whitenoise-rs as the source of truth for the Rust core.

Stats: 304 files changed, 469 insertions, 47,854 deletions (mostly the deleted wrapper and generated dart bindings).

## Verified

- `flutter pub get` resolves the new git dep cleanly (1 dep changed).
- `flutter analyze`: No issues found.
- Dart import rewrite: zero residual `package:whitenoise/src/rust` references across `lib/` and `test/`.

## Coordination with whitenoise-rs

This PR pairs with marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs#827, and order of merge matters: the whitenoise-rs PR lands (or its workflow runs via `workflow_dispatch`) so the `flutter-package` orphan branch contains the latest published package, then this PR can merge. Otherwise `flutter pub get` resolves an outdated snapshot. The wrapper sources in the orphan branch came from this branch's `rust/src/api/` (the singleton-removal refactor that is also in this branch's history).

## Why draft

The Android build script needs the follow-up above, and a manual smoke test of `flutter pub get` and `flutter analyze` from a clean clone is still pending before this is ready for review.

The colony has split the work across two burrows: one builds the bindings, the other consumes them. Less paw-ferrying for everyone.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Documentation**
  * Clarified agent setup and dependency flow; added steps to refresh the Rust core consumed as a published Flutter package; updated Android/native build guidance.

* **Chores**
  * Switched native/Rust integration to a published Flutter package; simplified development and CI workflows to run Flutter-only dependency/install/test steps.

* **Refactor**
  * Updated app imports to use the new published Rust-backed Flutter package.

* **Breaking Changes**
  * Removed the autogenerated native↔Flutter bridge surface and related native build glue; upgrade/migration required.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
